blocks.text: Q-Line Biotech is a Lucknow-based in-vitro diagnostics (IVD) company that makes and trades diagnostic reagents, analysers, lab consumables and service contracts for laboratories, hospitals and government health programmes [F] (RATING; AR2026 p.49). It earns money in two ways. It sells or places analysers, often at or near cost, and then sells the reagents those analysers use every day. Management calls this a razor-blade model [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Consolidated FY26 revenue was Rs 341.7 cr, EBITDA Rs 98.1 cr (28.7%) and PAT Rs 55.7 cr [F] (AR2026 p.161; PPT Jun 2026).

items: End markets: about 65% of revenue is business-to-government (B2G) and 35% is trade (private labs, lab chains, hospitals) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The company does not break down end markets by hospital, lab or POC.

Geography: North India is 84% of revenue, Uttar Pradesh about 77% and exports 0.3% [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Management says the UP share reflects billing to one UP-based distributor that supplies government labs in Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha and Haryana [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

Customer profile: one promoter-group partnership firm, POCT Services, bought Rs 225.88 cr of goods in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.75; AR2026 p.184). That is about 66% of consolidated revenue [E] (AR2026 p.161). CARE puts POCT Services at about 44% of sales [F] (RATING). **The two figures are not reconciled.**
Manufactured products were 67.4% of FY26 revenue, up from 54.0% in FY25. Traded products fell 23% [F] (AR2026 p.83; AR2026 p.188).

subsections.title: Listing status and what it means for the evidence base

blocks.text: The shares listed on NSE Emerge (the SME platform) on 29 May 2026. The IPO was a fresh issue of 62,53,200 shares at Rs 343 raising Rs 214.48 cr, after a pre-IPO placement of 8,00,000 shares at Rs 343 (Rs 27.44 cr) [F] (AR2026 p.51). FY26 is therefore the first annual report as a listed company. The June 2026 call was the company's first earnings call [F] (CALL Jun 2026). SME companies report half-yearly, so our model quarterly columns labelled 'Mar 2025' and 'Mar 2026' are actually the H2FY25 and H2FY26 half-years (sales Rs 217 cr and Rs 198 cr match the half-year table) [F] (NUMBERS; PPT Jun 2026).

Evidence gaps: the prospectus was not available in this folder. The standalone financial statements and standalone auditor's report (AR2026 pp.100-149) are image-only in the text version and could not be read. our model holds only four annual years. The earlier dashboard note (BOARD) calls the company 'debt-free', but consolidated borrowings were Rs 225 cr at March 2026 [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.160). Treat BOARD as unverified.

subsections.title: Bear thesis: reasons not to own it

items: 1. A promoter firm is the main customer. POCT Services, a partnership in which a director is a partner, bought Rs 225.88 cr in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.75; AR2026 p.183), about 66% of revenue [E] (AR2026 p.161). CARE's figure is about 44% [F] (RATING). Related-party sales are priced partly on 'idle capacity at plant' and 'future prospect of recurring business' [F] (AR2026 p.185), which is flexible enough to move margin between the listed company and the promoter firm [AI].

2. Profits have not turned into cash. Over three years operating cash flow was -0.08x PAT and cumulative free cash flow was Rs -149 cr [F] (NUMBERS). FY26 CFO was Rs 16 cr against PAT of Rs 56 cr [F] (NUMBERS).

3. Receivables are stretching. Debtor days went from 96 to 134 and trade receivables from Rs 82.6 cr to Rs 125.8 cr [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.179). About Rs 72.9 cr is shown as outstanding from related parties, but the column alignment in the extracted note is imperfect [F] (AR2026 p.184).

4. Guarantees for the group are rising. Contingent corporate guarantees for group entities total about Rs 46 cr at March 2026, on our reading of the note (the FY25 column is not cleanly legible) [F] (AR2026 p.182). Management said on the call that these are being wound down, with no timeline [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). CARE lists additional group guarantees as a negative rating trigger [F] (RATING).

5. Accounting choices flatter EBITDA. The company capitalises R&D (Rs 4.68 cr added to R&D assets in FY26) and 'contract acquisition cost', including customer discounts (Rs 10.82 cr gross block) [F] (AR2026 p.168; AR2026 p.177). The Directors' Report shows R&D expense of only Rs 22.13 lakh [F] (AR2026 p.66).

6. Governance is weak. Ayush Garg, the promoter's 24-year-old son and a Non-Executive Director, was the highest-paid person at Rs 1.61 cr and sits on the audit committee [F] (AR2026 p.79; AR2026 p.77; AR2026 p.55). The audit committee met only twice in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.55).

7. The audit is thin. The auditor is a proprietorship first appointed in September 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.50; AR2026 p.157). It relied on management's own list of related parties and promoters [F] (AR2026 p.179; AR2026 p.184) and reported no key audit matters [F] (AR2026 p.152).

8. Growth is uneven. FY26 revenue grew 9%, H2FY26 revenue fell 9% year on year and instrument revenue fell 28% [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [E]. FY25's 55% jump relied on a one-off government instrument-seeding programme [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

9. The price assumes far more than history. At Rs 726 the share is about 3x the base DCF (Rs 242.6) and above the bull DCF (Rs 382.9). The price implies 45.4% annual sales growth for five years [F] (NUMBERS).

10. The evidence base is inconsistent. FY25 PAT is Rs 28 cr in NUMBERS versus Rs 19.2 cr in the annual report; FY25 CFO is Rs -1 cr versus Rs +17.2 cr; R&D spend is Rs 22 lakh versus Rs 2.5-5 cr; CARE calls the company 'erstwhile Poct Services Private Limited' [F] (NUMBERS; AR2026 p.161; AR2026 p.162; RATING; CALL Jun 2026).

blocks.text: The market price treats Q-Line as a manufacturing-led IVD compounder, trading at 30.2x trailing earnings and 19.6x EV/EBITDA [F] (NUMBERS). Our read is that the business is better described as a captive supplier to a promoter-controlled government lab-services firm. It is moving towards manufacturing, and that is genuinely improving gross margin, but its revenue, receivables and guarantees remain entangled with the promoter group [AI]. The upside variant is that disclosed margins are real and the IPO lets the company fund the working capital that government supply needs. If trade revenue reaches 50% by FY28 as management guides [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), the concentration discount could narrow. The downside variant is that three years of negative free cash flow [F] (NUMBERS), rising receivables and capitalised costs mean reported profit overstates distributable earnings. On that view even our model bull case (Rs 382.9 per share) sits well below the price [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: The manufacturing business is much newer than the 2010 incorporation suggests. Selectra Pro M manufacturing started only in December 2023 and Unit 4 in February 2026 [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Manufactured instrument revenue was Rs 6.1 cr in FY24 [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Until recently, management says, reagents were '100%' traded and imported [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The group was restructured in March 2025, just before the listing process: an associate was sold at a loss, a subsidiary was sold and another acquired, and the company converted to public status [F] (AR2026 p.164; AR2026 p.181; AR2026 p.188). Most of the board, the CFO and the CS joined in 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.53). **In effect the investable history of the current manufacturing-led company is about two years, and its governance apparatus is about one year old** [AI].

subsections.title: Production and service chain, step by step

items: Step 1, inputs: raw materials, reagents, components and whole instruments are bought, some imported. Import purchases rose from Rs 19.49 cr in FY24 to Rs 56.49 cr in FY26 [F] (RATING).

Step 2, R&D and technology transfer: reagents are developed in-house through a DSIR-approved R&D centre [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Instruments come via technology transfer (Vital Scientific, Boule Sweden AB, Stago) [F] (PPT Jun 2026).

Step 3, manufacturing: four units. Delhi makes clinical chemistry, molecular and rapid/ELISA kits; Lucknow Units 2-4 make haematology reagents, instruments and POC devices, and clinical chemistry, rapid and glucometer products [F] (PPT Jun 2026). The mapping of products to units is read from a garbled slide [AI].
Step 4, regulatory approval: CDSCO licences are needed product by product. Unit 4 holds licences for five products, with more under review [F] (PPT Jun 2026).

Step 5, distribution: more than 75 distributors across India [MC] (CALL Jun 2026), led by the related party POCT Services for government supply [F] (AR2026 p.184). Direct sales operations in South and West India started in 2026 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).
Step 6, instrument placement: analysers are sold to government or distributors at roughly hardware-cost recovery, or placed on lease [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).
Step 7, recurring pull-through: reagent sales for 8-10 years per analyser, plus AMC service revenue [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

subsections.title: Where value is captured and why

blocks.text: Value sits in reagents. Management cites gross margins of 60-65% on manufactured reagents, about 50% on traded reagents and 15-20% on manufactured instruments [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The audited segment data agree on direction: manufacturing earned a segment result of Rs 115.4 cr on Rs 230.2 cr revenue (50.1%) and trading Rs 44.2 cr on Rs 111.5 cr (39.6%), both before Rs 56.8 cr of unallocated costs [F] (AR2026 p.188) [E]. Part of the value is captured at the POCT Services level, which buys from Q-Line and provides end-to-end lab services to government hospitals [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). How that margin is split is not disclosed and cannot be tested [AI].

Fixed assets plus CWIP rose from Rs 35 cr in FY23 to Rs 160 cr in FY26, and fixed-asset turnover fell from 7.96x to 2.36x [F] (NUMBERS). The heavier burden is working capital: inventories of Rs 95.0 cr and receivables of Rs 125.8 cr against payables of Rs 52.0 cr at March 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.178; AR2026 p.179; AR2026 p.174). Net trade working capital was about Rs 168.7 cr, or 49% of revenue [E]. Instruments are sold rather than given free, so Q-Line does not tie up capital in placed analysers the way many IVD peers do, but it accepts longer receivables instead [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). We classify the model as moderately asset-heavy in fixed assets and highly working-capital-intensive [AI].

blocks.text: Exports are immaterial today. The company appointed a Dubai-based international business manager, signed distributor agreements in 7-8 countries and registered products in the Middle East, Africa and Mauritius [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The segment note says geographical segments are not reported because operations are 'entirely within India' [F] (AR2026 p.188). The 5x FY27 export target would still leave exports at roughly Rs 6 cr, under 2% of FY26 revenue [E] (PPT Jun 2026). **Exports are a strategy statement, not yet a revenue mix change** [AI].

items: Import dependence: imports were Rs 56.49 cr in FY26 (Rs 19.49 cr in FY24), partly hedged with forward contracts [F] (RATING).
Foreign-currency trade payables: USD 38.70 lakh (Rs 36.63 cr) and EUR 4.08 lakh (Rs 4.45 cr) at March 2026 [F] (AR2026 p.185), about 79% of total trade payables of Rs 52.04 cr [E] (AR2026 p.174).
Foreign-currency spend on royalty and technology fees is disclosed, but amounts in the extracted note are not reliably legible [F] (AR2026 p.185).

Tariff and trade policy: none of the documents discuss specific tariff measures or dates. Exposure is not disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.81; RATING). Government 'Make in India' and PLI schemes are cited as tailwinds, without any company-specific incentive amount [F] (PPT Jun 2026).

subsections.title: 1. Installed-base reagent annuity (Selectra Pro M and haematology)

blocks.text: Position in the value chain: Q-Line localises assembly of partner-designed analysers and makes the consumable reagents [F] (PPT Jun 2026). What exists today: 1,550 Selectra units installed since December 2023 manufacturing began, 1,053 haematology analysers added, and reagent revenue up 35% [F] (PPT Jun 2026) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). What is narrative: Rs 3 lakh per analyser per year and Rs 30 lakh lifetime value [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Management itself says consumption varies widely by analyser type (about Rs 4,000/month for haematology, 'multiple lakhs' for immunology) [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Only about 450 Selectra units were actively ordering reagents in FY26 [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Cumulative manufactured-instrument revenue (FY24-FY26) of about Rs 106.5 cr over 1,550 units implies about Rs 6.9 lakh per unit [E] (PPT Jun 2026), below the Rs 10-20 lakh list range quoted for fully automatic analysers [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). That suggests heavy discounting or a mix of lower-priced units [AI].

items: FY24 (EBITDA margin 18% to 19%): Selectra manufacturing began in December 2023 with only Rs 6.1 cr of manufactured instruments [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Gross margin improved 270 bp [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Assessment: early structural signal, too small to judge [AI].

FY25 (to 22.5% per the annual report): revenue +54% on a government instrument-seeding programme [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Gross margin dipped to 53.3% as low-margin instruments grew, while operating leverage lifted EBITDA margin [F] (PPT Jun 2026). About Rs 10.8 cr of contract acquisition cost was capitalised instead of expensed [F] (AR2026 p.177; AR2026 p.180). Assessment: largely temporary (volume spike plus capitalisation) [AI].

FY26 (to 28.7%): mix shift to manufactured reagents, gross margin +750 bp [F] (AR2026 p.87). Employee costs rose 32% but other expenses only 5% [F] (AR2026 p.161) [E]. Rs 4.68 cr of R&D was capitalised [F] (AR2026 p.177). Assessment: mostly structural mix shift, partly helped by lower instrument mix (temporary) and capitalisation (accounting) [AI].

H2FY26 (31.4%): gross margin 62.9% on a lower instrument share; revenue -9% [F] (PPT Jun 2026). Assessment: peak-mix half; H1FY25 already showed a 65.2% gross margin, which then fell away [E] (PPT Jun 2026).

blocks.text: Partly. The manufacturing segment margin rose from 44.4% to 50.1% [E] (AR2026 p.188), so the reagent mix shift is real. Three things argue against extrapolating the 28.7%. Second, the instrument share that depressed margins in FY25 is guided to recover with 2,000 placements [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Third, capitalised R&D and customer costs flatter EBITDA by several crore [F] (AR2026 p.177). our model base case already assumes 24% EBITDA margin rather than 29% [F] (NUMBERS). **We regard 24-27% as the defensible through-cycle range until H1FY27 proves otherwise** [AI].
